title: Who owns what
lede: Four placeholder members each own use-case models and at least one design problem, with Member C covering both cycle and Archive.
intro: Member A, Member B, Member C and Member D are placeholders for names the team will fill in. This is the agreed presentation and study allocation, not a claim about historical authorship, effort or commit ownership.

The course requires each member to explain at least one use case at both analysis and design levels and at least one problem solved using a pattern. Prepare the analysis class view, an analysis sequence for each major flow, the design class view and the matching design sequences. For the design problem, prepare the brute-force alternative, candidates, choice, before/after class and sequence views, and implementation decisions.

The suggested two-minute outlines below introduce each member’s part; they do not replace the full use-case discussion or demonstration. Existing report SVGs need the current-code reading notes in [analysis to design](analysis-design.html) and [patterns](patterns.html), especially for Cognito, browser retro processing, recurring reminders and renamed modules.

sections.title: The agreed ownership split
sections.summary: ACCESS belongs to A, CAPTURE to B, CYCLE and ARCHIVE to C, and PARTICIPATION to D.
paragraphs: Each member has a primary use case to lead with and a bounded design problem to explain. The wider assigned use cases still need their class and major-flow sequence models; the lead case is a rehearsal starting point.

Overlapping flows are shared interfaces, not competing ownership: A explains invitation membership and session trust; C explains how a link carries invitation intent. A explains access to settings; D explains prompt/timezone and reminder behaviour. B explains the accepted contribution; C explains how durable jobs consume it and release a film.

qa.q: Are these the confirmed real names and historical contributions?
qa.a: No. They are placeholders and an agreed study/presentation allocation. The team must fill in names and separately evidence actual effort.

qa.q: Does Member C need to present two problems?
qa.a: C owns two report packages here, so prepares both lifecycle recovery and private Archive delivery. Each other member also has a specific problem, meeting the minimum one per member.

sections.title: Member A · ACCESS
sections.summary: Own the path from verified sign-in to a private group: UC01–UC03, with UC03 invitation acceptance as a clear lead use case.
paragraphs: **Package and use cases:** ACCESS. UC01 — Register, authenticate and manage a session; UC02 — Create and select a real group; UC03 — Issue, revoke and accept a group invitation. Explain Cognito Managed Login on web/PWA and configuration-gated developer password sign-in. Both end in Rewind sessions; group membership is a separate decision.

**Design problem and pattern:** [trusted identity without duplicated route policy](patterns.html#access). Present Adapter at the provider/request boundary plus explicit authorisation functions. The older mixed Demo/real Strategy discussion is historical. There is no universal Strategy class in today’s policy module.

**Lead use-case models:** [analysis class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/uc03-analysis-class.svg) · [design class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/uc03-design-class.svg); find every major-flow analysis/design sequence in the [model register](analysis-design.html#sequence-model-register).

**Before/after problem models:** [before class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/problem-before-class.svg) · [before sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/problem-before-sequence.svg) · [older after class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/problem-after-class.svg) · [older after sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/access/diagrams/problem-after-sequence.svg). The old after view retains removed Demo participants; use the [current boundary explanation](analysis-design.html#t1-trusted-identity) to explain the change.

**Code to know:** the provider/client restore session state; auth routes coordinate Cognito and developer login; `CognitoService` adapts the provider; group/invite functions own membership decisions; media identity helpers bind the selected group/profile.
notes: **Suggested 0:00–0:20:** define Account versus a group’s Membership/Profile. An invitation code is bounded joining intent, not an authenticated identity.
**0:20–0:50:** walk UC03 analysis: invitee boundary → invitation control → Invitation, Group and Membership entities; show valid and expired/replayed flows.
**0:50–1:20:** map the control to `acceptRealGroupInvite`; explain session resolution, expiry/replay/capacity checks and transactional membership creation.
**1:20–1:45:** compare route-local checks with the current sign-in Adapter and explicit policy boundaries. Describe Cognito state/nonce/PKCE before the Rewind session.
**1:45–2:00:** show a denial branch and hand the accepted member/group context to B’s capture flow.

qa.q: Why not authorise using memberId from the request?
qa.a: The client can change it. The server derives identity from the session and resolves the account’s group membership/profile.

qa.q: How does Cognito differ from group authorisation?
qa.a: Cognito establishes who signed in. Rewind decides which groups and owner operations that account may access.

qa.q: How do you stop an invitation being used twice?
qa.a: Acceptance rechecks persisted invite state inside the membership transaction and records acceptance with the resulting membership.

qa.q: What changed from your older design diagram?
qa.a: The Demo identity family was removed and Cognito was implemented. The current design converges sign-in into Rewind sessions and keeps explicit real-account membership checks.

sections.title: Member B · CAPTURE
sections.summary: Own photo/video capture through accepted contribution: UC04–UC06, with UC04 as the lead use case.
paragraphs: **Package and use cases:** CAPTURE. UC04 — Record, review, trim and submit video; UC05 — Contribute a photo; UC06 — Enforce allowance and one correction. Cover permission, review/retake, upload interruption, duplicate submission, processing failure and correction rejection as well as success.

**Design problem and pattern:** [contain capture, processing and transfer variation](patterns.html#capture). Present Adapter contracts for camera, local files and runtime transport. Describe sessions and extracted hooks as the actual coordinators; do not claim an inheritance-based Template Method.

**Lead use-case models:** [analysis class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/uc04-analysis-class.svg) · [design class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/uc04-design-class.svg); find every major-flow analysis/design sequence in the [model register](analysis-design.html#sequence-model-register).

**Before/after problem models:** [before class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/problem-before-class.svg) · [before sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/problem-before-sequence.svg) · [after class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/problem-after-class.svg) · [older after sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/capture/diagrams/problem-after-sequence.svg). Add the current pre-upload browser retro stage and split hooks when explaining the older after view.

**Code to know:** `CameraPlatform` abstracts device capture; recording/review sessions own the local workflow; upload hooks prepare retro media and manage cancellation; the runtime client handles direct/staged transfer; server quota and ledger operations decide acceptance and correction. The UI’s allowance is advisory.
notes: **Suggested 0:00–0:20:** state the problem: the same capture intent crosses device APIs, local media, an unreliable network and server limits.
**0:20–0:50:** walk UC04 analysis through capture, review and submit; identify the boundary, coordinating control and Recording/Contribution entities.
**0:50–1:20:** map to CameraPlatform, review/upload sessions and hooks. Explain supported browser retro preparation before transfer and server fallback where required.
**1:20–1:45:** compare the brute-force screen with the Adapter seams. Show how idempotency and the server’s quota transaction handle a lost upload response.
**1:45–2:00:** explain one correction/cancellation branch and hand the persisted contribution/job to C.

sources.note: Preparation, retro, upload and processing states.

qa.q: Who stops two simultaneous uploads exceeding allowance?
qa.a: The server’s atomic count/duration reservation, not the screen’s displayed remaining count.

qa.q: What if the user retries after the response disappears?
qa.a: Reuse the idempotency key and reconcile the existing contribution rather than consuming another allowance.

qa.q: Is the retro look always done on the phone?
qa.a: The web photo path does it locally; web video does when re-encoding is supported. Otherwise the server applies the look. A processed flag avoids double grading.
It is not implemented as a base class with overridden steps. Capture uses Adapter contracts, sessions and hooks.

sections.title: Member C · CYCLE and ARCHIVE
sections.summary: Own accepted contribution to released film and authorised playback: UC07, UC08 and UC12–UC14, with UC08 as the lead case.
paragraphs: **Packages and use cases:** CYCLE — UC07 Close a cycle and open its successor; UC08 Compile, retry, publish, premiere and archive a film. ARCHIVE — UC12 View premiere and released Archive; UC13 Download own clip or group film; UC14 Install, update and open an invitation. Explain iOS as the PWA, and keep invitation intent separate from A’s server membership decision.

**Design problem 1:** [recoverable cycle/film work](patterns.html#cycle). Present a persisted state machine and durable command-like jobs, with transactions, leases and generation fencing. There are no State/Command subclass families.

**Design problem 2:** [private Archive delivery](patterns.html#archive). Present the capability-gated Proxy role, supported by the archive client Facade and download Adapters. Media-store references name bytes; current membership and release state authorise delivery.

**Lead use-case models:** [analysis class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/uc08-analysis-class.svg) · [design class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/uc08-design-class.svg); find every major-flow analysis/design sequence in the [model register](analysis-design.html#sequence-model-register). Supporting playback case: [UC12 analysis class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/uc12-analysis-class.svg) · [UC12 design class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/uc12-design-class.svg).

**Cycle problem models:** [before class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/problem-before-class.svg) · [before sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/problem-before-sequence.svg) · [after class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/problem-after-class.svg) · [after sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/cycle/diagrams/problem-after-sequence.svg). **Archive problem models:** [before class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/problem-before-class.svg) · [before sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/problem-before-sequence.svg) · [after class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/problem-after-class.svg) · [after sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/archive/diagrams/problem-after-sequence.svg). Read older SQLite and screen labels using the current source paths below.

**Code to know:** lifecycle functions record transitions, successor and publication; jobs record inputs and current claim; the worker runs FFmpeg; capabilities and serving routes recheck access; Film refreshes media before download; the PWA worker caches public shell assets only. PostgreSQL is implemented behind the database Adapter, rather than being future architecture.
notes: **Suggested 0:00–0:20:** draw the story: collecting cycle → revealing/processing → published premiere → archived; the next cycle can already collect.
**0:20–0:50:** use UC08 analysis to separate compilation, retry and publication; show the design’s durable job/input records and worker claim.
**0:50–1:15:** compare transient timer work with persisted state and generation-fenced finalisation. A repeated tick or crash must not create a new authoritative successor/result.
**1:15–1:45:** connect release to UC12/UC13: refresh media, issue a short-lived grant, recheck current session/group/release and verify bytes before serving. Explain Proxy versus Facade.
**1:45–2:00:** answer one stale-worker or expired-capability branch and identify the PWA cache boundary. Expand both package problems during the full presentation.

qa.q: How can the next cycle collect while the previous film is still compiling?
qa.a: Closing the old cycle and creating/selecting its successor are transactional lifecycle work. Compilation is a separate durable job, so a slow film does not keep intake on the old cycle.

qa.q: Why does a retry not let the old worker win?
qa.a: The current persisted claim generation must match at finalisation. A stale worker cannot overwrite a later claim.

qa.q: Why does the premiere last from publication rather than cycle end?
qa.a: Compilation may finish late. release_published_at starts the configured 24-hour premiere after verified output is actually published.

qa.q: What happens after a media capability expires or the process restarts?
qa.a: The client refreshes authorisation and requests a fresh grant. Durable media remains stored; serving still checks session, membership, release and exact output identity.

sections.title: Member D · PARTICIPATION
sections.summary: Own the group’s continuing interaction: UC09–UC11, with UC11 chat/reconnect as the lead use case.
paragraphs: **Package and use cases:** PARTICIPATION. UC09 — Owner prompt and group timezone; UC10 — Reminder preference and asynchronous delivery; UC11 — Private group chat. Cover owner-only settings, local scheduling, consent, disconnected chat, retries and stream access loss.

**Design problem and patterns:** [keep live chat and durable reminders truthful](patterns.html#participation). Present Observer/pub-sub for committed chat events, a provider Adapter for web push and a durable outbox for scheduled reminders. A live subscriber and a retryable reminder job are different responsibilities.

**Lead use-case models:** [analysis class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/uc11-analysis-class.svg) · [design class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/uc11-design-class.svg); find every major-flow analysis/design sequence in the [model register](analysis-design.html#sequence-model-register).

**Before/after problem models:** [before class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/problem-before-class.svg) · [before sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/problem-before-sequence.svg) · [after class](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/problem-after-class.svg) · [older after sequence](https://github.com/Collaboration95/rewind-app/blob/dev/doc/planning/report/packages/participation/diagrams/problem-after-sequence.svg). The recurring reminder loop now exists; the active product channel is web push. Replace older one-shot-only or Expo delivery claims when explaining the plates.

**Code to know:** chat functions commit message/event state; RealtimeHub fans out afterwards; SSE routes replay message events through a watermark; the realtime client reconnects. Reminder settings/destinations and outbox state persist separately; the runtime loop scans/drains when providers are configured. Reaction updates do not advance the message reconnect cursor.
notes: **Suggested 0:00–0:20:** separate live conversation from scheduled reminders. Both are asynchronous, but only one is a connected subscriber.
**0:20–0:50:** use UC11 analysis: chat boundary → conversation control → Message/Event; identify history, send/reply, reaction and reconnect major flows.
**0:50–1:20:** map to transactional chat functions, hub and SSE client. Explain commit-before-publish, watermark replay and buffered live events.
**1:20–1:45:** compare an observer-only reminder design with preference, destination generation, durable outbox, lease and web-push Adapter.
**1:45–2:00:** distinguish queued, provider-accepted and observed display, then show how disabling a destination invalidates stale work.

sources.note: Destination generation, eligibility, lease and outcomes.

qa.a: A live event must correspond to a committed message. If the connection drops, the client can recover the committed message from event replay.

qa.q: How do you avoid a gap while replay meets live traffic?
qa.a: Subscribe and buffer while taking a watermark, replay persisted message events through it, then flush newer buffered events once.

qa.q: How does opting out affect pending work?
qa.a: Preference and destination eligibility are rechecked; disabling a destination increments its generation so stale queued work cannot use that destination.

qa.q: Does the reminder scheduler now recur automatically?
qa.a: The runtime starts a bounded recurring loop when providers are configured. This proves the mechanism exists, not that a particular device displayed a notification.
